findings.summary: One function spells the runtime query bag (`searchParamsValue`, with the type name taken from the data-type registry); the runtime constructor path and the deployment bag both call it.
`hasNativeSpelling` names the browser values a native read can spell (primitives and the deployment bag) beside `isPrimitiveBrowserValue`, whose helper-argument use keeps the primitive-only meaning.

The deployment bag materializes only where a read the fold cannot answer arrives, inside the data-method dispatch, as a function-local static parsed once per emitting function (under workers each read parses its own); an eager materialization at every value read cost a parse per read and turned a bag bound through a conditional native, unfolding its later literal-key reads.

The dispatch keys that hook on the owner value being a browser bag, so a module-level bag bound as browser state and an unbound one inside a native function both parse at the read; keyed on the binding miss alone, a module-level runtime-key read refused.
The query argument pin is skipped for a plain name; only a computed key is pinned.

The fixture keeps the shapes that reach the native path: an arrow helper and a function helper read runtime keys from a loop inside a function, a module-level loop reads runtime keys through the bound bag, with one literal call and one `has` fold beside them; the defaulted-flag helper, the vector helper and the literal calls that fold on main and branch alike are gone.

The owner routing keeps its kind list rather than compiling every unbound identifier through the value lowering, which would turn constant arrays and records into dynamic owners that the constant-array paths own.
The mechanism is described once, at the shared spelling; the other sites point to it.
One namespace-level constant per query string would parse once per program and give `qs === qs` its JavaScript identity across functions.
findings.blockedBy: The function-local static already parses once per emitting function, the compiler has no module-constant emission path for a GC container, and no scene compares query bags by identity.
findings.filedIn: docs/features.md (URLSearchParams limits: a deployment bag parsed for a runtime key is one per function, not one object)

findings.summary: Spelling the bag at the value level, with the constructor arm no longer skipping an answered `new URLSearchParams`, would also pass the bag to helpers and let `hasBrowserInput` use `hasNativeSpelling`.
findings.blockedBy: A bag declared through a conditional (`typeof location !== "undefined" ? new URLSearchParams(location.search) : null`) would then bind natively and its literal-key reads would stop folding, which the host-location-guard fixture pins; folding conditional expressions over answered browser values is the deeper change.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md (the classification consolidation entry) and docs/features.md (URLSearchParams limits: a bag passed to a helper stays browser state)

findings.summary: `compileStaticContainer` could compile any module constant initialized with a constructor through the value lowering, so a module `new Date(0)` read in a helper would lower too and the kind list would return to strings.
findings.blockedBy: Compiling a constructor at each use forks the state of a class instance or mutable container built there; only immutable constructors may be re-materialized, which needs a constructor whitelist or a module-constant emission path.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md (the classification consolidation entry: a module constant initialized with a constructor compiled once instead of at each use)
